gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Elite 30 V2's '1500W Lifting Power' is, in BLUETTI's own words, a momentary figure for 'pure resistive devices' only, or that Jackery's 4,000-cycle rating on the Explorer 300 runs to 70% capacity while BLUETTI and Anker give 3,000 cycles with no capacity endpoint on their own US pages.
standout_why: I read three pages. PowerSized (powersized.com/solar-generator-kits, cited) has one 'Output (W)' column that doesn't say whether the number is rated or surge. It doesn't mention cycle life or Power Lifting. It does already make the panel-versus-input point ('Panel watts above the station's limit do not charge it any faster'), so that point isn't new. OffGridEmpire (cited) lists inverter watts without saying rated or surge, and only says 'LiFePO4 cycles 3,000+ times' with no endpoint. BLUETTI's EB3A page (cited) sells one product only. I couldn't open SolarGenAdvisor's under-$500 page (cited in the pin chat) because its TLS certificate failed, so I don't know what it says. ChatGPT's own answers repeat '600W AC' for the BLUETTI and 'LiFePO4' as a lifespan proxy. None of them separates rated, surge and Power Lifting, or gives cycle endpoints.
decides: This supports the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W as the pick, with a correction to how we state its output. Its real advantage is 600 W continuous against 300 W continuous on the Jackery Explorer 300 / 300 v2 and the Anker C300. The 1,500 W number is not surge headroom for motors or compressors, so our table cell '600 W (1,500 W Power Lifting)' needs a footnote saying it's resistive loads only and momentary. BLUETTI's pages publish no surge figure for the Elite 30 V2, while Jackery and Anker both publish 600 W surge. Jackery's '4,000+ cycles' looks better than 3,000, but it's measured to a looser 70% endpoint and can't be compared one-to-one. It shouldn't count as a durability win for the Jackery kit. Two other things change how the kits compare. Jackery says its SolarSaga 100 Air is 'not compatible with Explorer 300 v2, Explorer 300', so that kit can't be upgraded with Jackery's current 100 W panel. And on its own store the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W kit costs $531 before any code, which is over $500.
